Hi Ben / Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attaching a first-draft Mutual Action Plan (ACME_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf) focused on the POC scope. I pulled out the POC environment setup milestone into a separate page since it has a few technical dependencies we should align on. Key items under that milestone: 

- VPC peering and routing (ACME network <> Redwood POC VPC) — proposed owner: ACME network lead (please share contact)
- IP allowlists / NATed egress addresses for API calls — proposed owner: ACME network
- SSO / SAML integration (Azure AD) — ACME identity team + Redwood SE for metadata exchange
- Secrets & KMS (customer-managed KMS for production; temporary secrets for POC) — security review required

Proposed target close date for the POC environment milestone: 2026-06-30. Can you confirm owners and whether the date looks feasible?

Next steps I suggest: 
1) Networking sync (30 min) to exchange VPC IDs and confirm peering model
2) Exchange SAML metadata (I attached saml-metadata.xml) and validate IdP config
3) Security/Q review for KMS & audit log requirements

Please review the MAP draft and comment inline if anything needs changing. Once we have network contact, Nikhil can schedule the technical call.

Thanks —

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the MAP draft. Quick questions from our side: 
- For VPC peering, do you require cross-account peering or a VPN? Our infra team prefers peering but needs the precise requirements (route tables, asymmetrical routing constraints).
- Can you share the exact IP ranges Redwood will use for outbound egress so we can pre-configure allowlists?
- On KMS: our security team will want to know whether Redwood supports AWS KMS CMKs (we prefer to manage keys). What audit logging is available for key usage?

Also, Sarah will coordinate our identity team for SAML metadata (we use Azure AD). If you can confirm Redwood supports standard SAML 2.0 with Azure AD and provide the metadata file, that will help.

Cc'ing Nikhil to respond on the technical specifics.

Hi Ben / Sarah —

Happy to take technical ownership for the POC environment setup. Quick responses below: 

VPC peering model:
- Redwood can support either AWS VPC peering (cross-account) or a VPN peering model. For the POC we recommend VPC peering for lower latency. If you choose peering we'll need your VPC IDs, account ID(s), and preferred CIDR for routing. We'll provide a minimal route table change doc.

IP allowlist / egress IPs:
- For outbound API egress during POC we can use a stable NAT IP block. Typical egress CIDR(s) we use for POCs: 35.232.112.0/20 and 34.82.0.0/15. If you require specific single IPs we can allocate elastic NATs but need prior notice.

SAML / SSO:
- Redwood supports standard SAML 2.0 and has been integrated with Azure AD in previous POCs. I attached saml-metadata.xml for the Redwood SP config. Steps: exchange metadata, set up trust, and do a test sign-on. Dev (cc'd) will help validate claims mapping and user provisioning.

KMS & secrets:
- We support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS or GCP KMS). For the POC it's acceptable to use temporary secrets, but for production we recommend CMKs. Audit logging: AWS CloudTrail integration is available for key usage events; we can provide an example log export and scope.

Attachments: network-diagram.png, saml-metadata.xml

Ask: can you share your network lead contact (name + email) and two 30-min windows for a network sync this week? I can host a call and walk through the network diagram.

Thanks —
Nikhil Sharma
